subject: Mathematics
topic: Why Division by Zero Is Undefined
title: Why Division by Zero Is Undefined
summary: A calculator says ERROR for 12 ÷ 0 because no number times 0 gives 12. It is not infinity either.

notes.title: 06 – Why Division by Zero Is Undefined

keyPoints: Division undoes multiplication: a ÷ b = c means c × b = a.
**0 ÷ 0**: every c works → no single answer → undefined.
**Infinity is not a number**; near 0, 12/x runs to +∞ on one side and −∞ on the other.

blocks.p: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 because 4 × 3 = 12. So 12 ÷ 0 = c would need c × 0 = 12, but **every number × 0 = 0**. No c exists.

blocks.alt: Several numbers multiplied by zero all give zero, never 12
blocks.caption: Whatever goes in, × 0 gives 0.

blocks.alt: Graph of 12 divided by x near zero going up on the right and down on the left
blocks.caption: Two opposite directions, so no single value.

blocks.p: That is why a rational number p/q needs **q ≠ 0**.

options: Every number works, so there is no single answer
quiz.explain: c × 0 = 0 for every c, so no unique value.
The denominator x − 3 is 0 when x = 3.

simulation.reason: A proof-by-reasoning idea: the multiplication check and the 12/x graph in the video and notes carry it fully; a slider would only repeat the graph.
